presenceLabel: Illinois (Illiniwek) town or declared claim in this area
presenceNote: The story is an event of 1778 (two town points, no boundary). The only sourced boundary is the claim the Kaskaskia declared on 13 Aug 1803: two river reaches can be drawn; the inland calls follow unlocated ridges and are not drawn, so no area is closed. No Kentucky territory is shown. The page spans 1778–1803 to include the 1803 claim.
overlapNote: Piankashaw (Wabash side: the 1804 treaty Art. 2 acknowledges the Kaskaskia right to sell their ceded country, separated from Piankashaw land by the Wabash/Saline Creek and Wabash/Mississippi-tributary divides), Kickapoo (took part of Illinois 'by conquest from the Illinois nation', 1819 treaty), Potawatomi and Miami to the north and east. Shawnee and Cherokee Kentucky claims do not overlap (west bank of the claim is the Ohio).
basis: Kaskaskia treaty 1803 (text), Piankeshaw treaty 1804 Art. 2, NPS Clark NHP page, Wikipedia coordinates for the towns.

eras.label: July–Sept 1778 · Clark at Cahokia and Kaskaskia
eras.text: Clark took Kaskaskia, Prairie du Rocher and Cahokia in July 1778, then held a council at Cahokia in late summer with leaders of nearby tribes; many accepted the white belt of peace, many others stayed allied with the British (NPS). The two towns are approximate points. No territory is drawn for this event.

eras.label: 1803 · The claim the Kaskaskia declared
eras.text: By 1803 the Illinois tribes (Kaskaskia, Michigamea, Cahokia, Tamaroa) were 'reduced to a very small number' and consolidated as the Kaskaskia. On 13 Aug 1803 at Vincennes they ceded their Illinois lands, reserving about 350 acres at Kaskaskia, and declared their claim: up the Ohio from the Mississippi to Saline Creek, then along watershed ridges to the Illinois River basin and the Illinois mouth, and down the Mississippi. Only the two river reaches are drawn, thin and dashed; the ridge calls are text only.

properties.note: Kaskaskia, Illinois (Wikipedia 37.9214, -89.9164). Clark took Kaskaskia, Prairie du Rocher and Cahokia in July 1778 (NPS). The Kaskaskia band and its chief Ducoigne were here; the 1803 treaty reserved about 350 acres near the town.

properties.note: Kaskaskia treaty 13 Aug 1803 Art. 5: the tribe declares its claim begins at the Ohio-Mississippi confluence, then up the Ohio to the mouth of Saline Creek, about twelve miles below the mouth of the Wabash. Drawn on the base-map Ohio centreline from Cairo up to the Wabash mouth plus twelve miles; thin dashed. The Ohio here is the Illinois-Kentucky state line.

Art. 5 closing call: a direct course to the mouth of the Illinois River, then down the Mississippi to the beginning (Cairo). Only the Mississippi reach (Cairo to the Illinois mouth) is drawn, on the base-map centreline, thin dashed. The middle calls follow unlocated dividing ridges (Saline Creek/Wabash, then Wabash/Kaskaskia/Illinois watersheds) and are NOT drawn, so there is no closed polygon.
Main-map extent: two sourced river reaches of the 1803 claim (dashed, never closed) and two town points. No Kentucky area is drawn.
